supported_findings: Both failures are last 64MiB x32 cell only; six streams received partial responses after successful requests and FIN.
OIC first terminal code is ChannelInterrupted with remote=false; OIS closing and closed record same code, not IdleTimeout.
Each channel joins exactly one target by reverse TCP tuples; target request FIN and first response Write succeeded, then target Write errored/reset.
The fixed diagnostics capture only first I/O boundaries; they do not record last failing operation, errno, last DATA progress, Ping result or transport-close origin.
Twelve cleanup measurements retain original baseline PIDs/exact Linux FDs and goroutine limits; failed Go leaves remain failed.
not_proven: Unique initiating component, syscall or internal terminal branch.
CPU/TCG scheduling, GC or Ping timeout as sole root cause.
Cross-process wall-clock differences as exact causal or monotonic intervals.
Target reset/write error as initiating fault rather than consequence of OIC reset.
Original gate or full formal run passing.
next_minimal_diagnostic: If authorized after preserving/sealing this run, add finite first-terminal diagnostics only: OIC failing operation (leg_read/leg_write/target_read/target_write), error class, local context/allow status; OIS leg role and read/write/ping completion/CloseNow origin.

Use original load, budgets and bounds; no blind retry, Ping/idle extension, GC sleep or weaker pass rule.

competing_mechanisms.mechanism: OIS Ping control Write deadline closes shared WebSocket transport
competing_mechanisms.distinction: pingLoop calls Ping before consulting activity/forwarding. Only timeout during acquired active frame Write installs setupWriteTimeout and closes the connection; waiting for pong or write lock timing out alone does not establish that close. No actual Ping/write-phase error was recorded.
